name: 23LC1024
full_name: Microchip 23LC1024 1Mbit (128K x 8) SPI Serial SRAM with SDI and SQI
description: The 23LC1024 is a 1 Mbit (128K x 8) serial SRAM accessed over SPI, with optional SDI (dual) and SQI (quad) modes, all running up to a 20 MHz clock. It operates from 2.5V to 5.5V, offers zero write time and unlimited read/write cycles, and supports byte, page (32-byte), and sequential transfer modes. Because it is SRAM, contents are volatile and lost on power-down. Its standout trait is providing fast, fatigue-free external RAM expansion over just a few SPI pins, ideal for buffering on RAM-starved microcontrollers.

pins.name: SO (SIO1)
pins.description: serial data output in SPI; SIO1 in SDI/SQI modes

pins.name: SIO2
pins.description: I/O line 2, used only in SQI (quad) mode

pins.name: SI (SIO0)
pins.description: serial data input in SPI; SIO0 in SDI/SQI modes

pins.name: /HOLD (SIO3)
pins.description: hold input (active low) in SPI/SDI; becomes SIO3 in SQI mode

typical_application: External volatile RAM buffer/scratchpad expansion for microcontrollers over SPI.
gotchas: it is SRAM, not flash/EEPROM; all data is lost on power loss, do not use for persistent storage
23LC1024 is the 2.5-5.5V part; the 23A1024 sibling is 1.7-2.2V only, do not mix them up on a 3.3V/5V rail
in basic SPI keep /HOLD high (or tie to VCC) or the device pauses; only release it intentionally
SIO2 and /HOLD-as-SIO3 are only active in SQI mode after switching the mode register; in plain SPI SIO2 is unused
default power-up mode is byte mode; set sequential or page mode in the mode register before relying on auto-increment
20 MHz clock ceiling (16 MHz for E-temp on 23A1024) is lower than typical flash, plan SPI bus speed accordingly
